subject: Plotting a Scalar on a Circular Domain

messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Plotting a Scalar on a Circular Domain
parts:
Dear All,
I do not know if ggplot2 is the right tool for this, but I need to plot
a scalar on a circle using a jet colormap.
Please consider a circle centered about the origin (0,0) of a system of
Cartesian coordinates and having radius R=pi/2.
Now, the function I would like to plot on the circle (and its interior)
is pretty simple

f(x,y)= abs(cos(x)),

which takes a value 1 at the equator and zero at the south/north Pole of
the circle.
On top of that, I would like to add some arrows/text to the figure (but
that is easy with ggplot2).

You can see a "hand made" example by visiting the link

http://dl.dropbox.com/u/5685598/first-plot_fixed.pdf

One thing which is far from clear to me is how to allow extra white
space around the circle to accommodate arrows and other text.
Any suggestion (also eventually about some other tool than ggplot2) is
welcome.
Many thanks

Lorenzo Isella

messages.author: 99a1cfc66539313c
messages.subject: Re: Plotting a Scalar on a Circular Domain
parts:
Lorenzo

Here you go:

library(ggplot2)

radius <- 1
resolution <- 0.01
# construct grid

cgrid <- expand.grid(x=seq(-radius, radius, resolution), y=seq(-
radius, radius, resolution))
cgrid$incircle <- ((cgrid$x^2 + cgrid$y^2) <= radius^2)
cgrid <- cgrid[cgrid$incircle==TRUE, ]

# add colour

cgrid$colour <- abs(cos(cgrid$x/radius))
str(cgrid)

p <- ggplot(cgrid, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
geom_tile(aes(fill=colour)) +
scale_fill_gradient(low="red", high="blue")

print(p)

--

Andrie
